title: Smooth locus of a flat morphism of algebraic spaces and arbitrary base change
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to T$ a flat locally finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For spaces, flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism], local finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and smoothness are tested on etale scheme charts, with scheme smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There is a largest open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace] $W\subset X$ such that $f|_W$ is smooth. For every morphism $h:T'\to T$ of schemes, with $p:X\times_TT'\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], the smooth locus of $f_{T'}$ is exactly $p^{-1}(W)$. In particular $f_{T'}$ is smooth if and only if $p^{-1}(X\setminus W)$ is empty. No properness or bound on fibre dimension is required.

source.place: Tag 02V4 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-smooth), case (1), and Tag 01V9 (lemma-smooth-at-point), transported to algebraic spaces by etale scheme charts; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0DZI (lemma-where-smooth) supplies the source-local construction, although its displayed base-change clauses alone only cover flat changes of base.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $q:U\to X$ from [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By the chart meanings in the statement, $a=fq:U\to T$ is flat and locally finitely presented. Let $V\subset U$ be the union of all open subschemes on which $a$ is smooth. The collection is a set of opens of $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source], $a|_V$ is smooth, including when this union is empty. Thus $V$ is exactly the set of points where $a$ is smooth. The restriction $q|_V$ is representable etale: on each scheme test it is an open immersion followed by an etale map, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], its image defines an open subspace $W\subset X$ and $V\to W$ is representable surjective etale.

To check smoothness of $f|_W$ on every etale scheme chart, let $Z\to W$ be such a chart. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $P=Z\times_WV$ is a scheme, $P\to Z$ is surjective etale, and $P\to V$ is etale. The pointwise clause of [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness] applied to $P\to V$ shows that $P\to T$ is smooth at every point, since $a|_V$ is smooth. Neighbourhoods witnessing this cover $P$, so [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] gives smoothness of $P\to T$. The covering clause of [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness], now applied to the surjective etale map $P\to Z$, gives smoothness of $Z\to T$. This verifies the chart meaning of smoothness of $f|_W$ without assuming an algebraic-space locality theorem as an extra black box.

If $B\subset X$ is any open subspace on which $f$ is smooth, the scheme $U_B=U\times_XB$ is an open of $U$ by [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Its composite to $T$ is smooth by the chart meaning of smoothness on $B$, so $U_B\subset V$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $U_B\to B$ is surjective etale. Its point image therefore shows $|B|\subset|W|$; [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] identifies this with $B\subset W$ as open subfunctors. Along with step 2 this proves that $W$ is the largest smooth open. This construction and maximality argument use no flatness, and consequently also apply to any base-changed morphism.

For any $h:T^{\prime}\to T$, form $X^{\prime}=X\times_TT^{\prime}$ and $U^{\prime}=U\times_TT^{\prime}$. Associating fibre products identifies $U^{\prime}=U\times_XX^{\prime}$, so [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] makes $U^{\prime}\to X^{\prime}$ a surjective etale atlas. Write $b:U^{\prime}\to U$. The new scheme lemma [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change] applies to the original flat locally finitely presented scheme morphism $a:U\to T$: its smooth-point equivalence says that the smooth locus on $U^{\prime}$ is exactly $V^{\prime}=b^{-1}(V)$. Steps 1-3 applied with this atlas construct the smooth locus of $X^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}$ as the image open of $V^{\prime}\to X^{\prime}$. By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], formation of the image open of $V\to X$ commutes with this arbitrary base change. It is therefore $W\times_XX^{\prime}=p^{-1}(W)$. Associativity here follows directly from the fibre-product universal property: both iterated products classify a point of $U$, a point of $T^{\prime}$, and equality of their images in $T$.

proof.text: On points, $p^{-1}(X\setminus W)=X^{\prime}\setminus p^{-1}(W)$, by the elementwise definition of inverse image. By step 4 this is the complement of the new smooth locus. It is empty exactly when that locus has full point image, equivalently is all of $X^{\prime}$ by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. If the new morphism is smooth, maximality gives this equality; conversely equality gives smoothness from the smooth restriction to its locus. This proves the stated equivalence, including empty source and empty base change. No step uses properness or a dimension bound.
